Writing m_n=|𝒰_n|, the validated estimates give B(M_n,m_n)=o(1) and log₂(M_n²B(M_n,m_n))=o(n), so the finite-dimensional restricted bound is o(1). The family may have arbitrary geometry but must be prescribed independently of the selected codebook and have subexponential cardinality. title: Zero restricted minimax overhead for prescribed subexponential rank-one families

changeRationale: This new node preserves the judgment’s durable methodological consequence while making its quantifier restriction explicit. It is nested under the zero restricted-overhead theorem because that theorem is the sole supplied basis for excluding this particular lower-bound strategy.
summary: A sequence of prescribed rank-one orientation families 𝒰_n with ln|𝒰_n|=o(n), fixed independently of the codebook, cannot by itself witness a positive asymptotic universality price against every codebook at fixed positive rate: the corresponding restricted minimax quantity tends to zero. This excludes fixed finite, polynomial-size, and more generally subexponential-size lists as standalone lower-bound witnesses. It does not exclude exponentially large or continuous orientation families, codebook-dependent adversarial choices, higher-rank metrics, or incompatibility mechanisms not captured by one prescribed subexponential list, and it does not rule out a positive universality price for the full problem.
title: Limitation of prescribed subexponential rank-one witness families
